clue.text: Give employees a rise for raising standards

definitions.meaning: to jack up wages is to raise them, so jacking up the staff reads as giving the workforce an increase
a standard is a flag, and this is the pole a ship's flag is hoisted on

explanation.surface: A boss lifts morale by awarding a pay increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raising standards' sounds like improving quality; here standards are flags.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words, it is jack (raise) plus staff (workers); as one, it is the pole at a ship's bow that carries the jack flag.

clue.text: Novelist won't switch in place of Virginia

parts.note: Henry James was an American novelist

indicators.note: switch means the letters change places

explanation.surface: An author refuses to change his home state.
explanation.definitionFit: The first permanent English settlement in America, founded in 1607, is a historic site in that state.

clue.text: Transport carries a little weight

indicators.note: carries means one word holds another inside it

parts.note: a cart is a vehicle for transport

explanation.surface: A vehicle bears a light load.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of mass for gemstones, 200 milligrams, is a very small weight.

clue.text: Turners upset plans in the works?

definitions.meaning: tools that turn nuts and bolts
the idiom about throwing one into the works means wrecking a scheme

explanation.definitionFit: Wrenches turn nuts, and the idiom 'a spanner in the works' is a thing that disrupts plans.

clue.text: Deny being in a rage, holding information up

indicators.note: holding means one word contains another

parts.note: bate is British slang for a fit of temper

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means the word is read upwards

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Someone furious withholds the facts and won't own up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the information word over in a down clue; 'in a bate' is British slang for in a temper, so 'being in' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To renounce or refuse oneself something is to deny it.

clue.text: Time, for example, to raise issue

definitions.meaning: Old ... Time, the personification of time
issue means offspring, and raising offspring is what a dad does

explanation.definitionFit: Father Time personifies time, and as a verb it means to beget children.

clue.text: It always has 28 on 22

parts.note: replace the numbers with their entries: 28 gives royal pieces, 22 gives the words 'a board', so the game always has those royal pieces on a board

explanation.walkthrough: The clue only makes sense once 28 (two monarchs' pieces) and 22 (read as 'a board') are filled in.
explanation.definitionFit: The board game played with kings, queens and pawns always keeps both kings on the board until mate.

clue.text: Effectively treating smoking, perhaps

definitions.meaning: smoking is one way of preserving meat or fish

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both healing a patient and preserving food by salting or smoking.

clue.text: Rivalling Greek character in ecstasy

indicators.note: in means the Greek letter goes inside the word for ecstasy

parts.note: elation is great joy
mu is the twelfth Greek letter

explanation.surface: A Greek man in raptures competes with another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rivalling' is an adjective here, matched by a noun: emulation is the act of rivalling.
explanation.definitionFit: Striving to equal or outdo someone is competitive imitation.

clue.text: Cook takes this as a matter of course

indicators.note: cook means the letters are worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A chef accepts this dish as routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a matter of course' looks like 'routine', but means something served as a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A beef fillet is often served as the main dish of a meal.

clue.text: Return of unusual bad weather could ruin Jersey

indicators.note: the word for unusual comes back, so its letters are read right to left

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or unusual
rain is the bad weather

explanation.surface: Freak storms threaten the economy of a Channel Island.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey is not the island but a breed of dairy cow; the answer is an old cattle plague.
explanation.definitionFit: This infectious disease of cattle could wipe out a herd of the dairy breed from the Channel Islands.

clue.text: Subject to pain or utter confusion

indicators.note: confusion signals that the letters of the two words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A choice between physical suffering and total bewilderment.
explanation.definitionFit: To torment someone is to inflict deliberate agony on them, which is putting them through suffering.

clue.text: Saints ain't half changing this material

indicators.note: changing tells us those letters are rearranged
only half the letters of the phrase are used, the first five of its ten

explanation.surface: A remark that saints are only partly reformed characters.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half of SAINTSAINT is SAINT; 'changing' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossy woven fabric is a kind of cloth, a material used for dresses and ribbons.

clue.text: Note an inexperienced player

parts.note: green means new and inexperienced
a back is a defensive player in football or rugby

explanation.surface: A remark about a novice member of a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' is not a jotting or a musical note but a banknote.
explanation.definitionFit: A US dollar bill is nicknamed this, from the colour printed on its reverse, so it is a paper note.

clue.text: Think too much of pace of Lord's proceedings

parts.note: Lord's is the London cricket ground, and play there proceeds in overs of six balls
rate means speed or pace

explanation.surface: Musing about how fast a cricket match at Lord's is going.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the famous cricket ground in London; the over rate is the number of overs bowled per hour.
explanation.definitionFit: To overvalue something is to esteem it more highly than it deserves.

clue.text: Back from Vienna, I draw designs of a pre-war type

indicators.note: Back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An artist home from Austria shows off sketches in an old-fashioned style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' marks the letters as lying within the words, and 'Back' reads them right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: The reign of Edward VII and the years up to 1914 are the period before the First World War.

clue.text: Wasn't slow to be secretive in speech

indicators.note: in speech says we want a word that sounds like the one given, not one spelt that way

parts.note: to hide is to keep oneself or something concealed

explanation.surface: Someone moved quickly so as to keep their secrets when talking.
explanation.walkthrough: The old verb 'hie' means to hurry, so its past tense means went quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Its past tense means hastened or hurried, the opposite of dawdling.

clue.text: Mother gets a view of ornamental inlay

parts.note: dam is a mother, of animals
a scene is a view

explanation.surface: Mum gets a look at a decorated piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Metalwork inlaid with gold or silver in the style of Damascus is decorative inlay.

clue.text: Co-operate in quiet song and dance

parts.note: p is piano, quiet in music
a lay is a song or ballad
a ball is a dance

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to join in a soft song and a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to go along with others and work with them.

clue.text: Preventing start of slump — jolly good!

indicators.note: start of means take the first letter of the next word

parts.note: topping is old British slang for excellent

explanation.surface: Halting an economic decline would be splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: Halting or blocking something is keeping it from happening.

clue.text: Daily need of fresh direction

parts.note: fresh means new
S is south, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Every day we need a change of course.
explanation.definitionFit: Current affairs are what a daily paper exists to supply; readers want the latest reports every day.

clue.text: Put in a £1000 order for metal

indicators.note: order means the letters are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: the pound sign gives L, from the Latin libra
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Placing a large order for a metal at a cost of a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: '£1000' gives two pieces: L for the pound and M for thousand, shuffled with PUTINA.
explanation.definitionFit: A precious white element used in jewellery and catalytic converters is a metal.

clue.text: Pierce like the wind

parts.note: to bore is to pierce
as means like

explanation.surface: A gale cuts through someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Boreas is the Greek god of the north wind, and so the wind itself.

clue.text: A lot of businessmen prepared to travel

parts.note: a board of directors is a group of businessmen

explanation.surface: Executives are ready to go on a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, plane or train, you are set to go on the journey.

clue.text: Act as peacemaker with child trader

parts.note: to bar a row is to stop a quarrel, as a peacemaker does
a boy is a child

explanation.surface: A mediator works alongside a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: A barrow boy is a British street trader who sells fruit and veg from a cart.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller hawking goods from a handcart in a street market is a kind of trader.

clue.text: Note escape of fish

parts.note: B is a musical note
a leak is an escape of gas or water

explanation.surface: A remark about a fish getting away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escape' is a noun here, a leak, not the fish's getaway.
explanation.definitionFit: A small silvery freshwater species of carp family is a fish.

clue.text: Dubliner has heartless ways

parts.note: Pat is a stock name for an Irishman

indicators.note: heartless takes away the middle letter of the word it qualifies

explanation.surface: A man from Dublin is said to be cruel in his manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the A at the centre of HAS, leaving HS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracks or routes are both ways of getting somewhere.

clue.text: Caught at Waterloo setting off explosives?

definitions.meaning: Waterloo is a London railway station, where travellers catch their transport
a line of gunpowder laid as a fuse to fire a charge

explanation.definitionFit: Commuters board one at the London terminus, and a trail of powder that fires a mine has the same name.

clue.text: Old philosopher endlessly agreeing to differ

indicators.note: to differ hints that the remaining letters change their order
endlessly means the last letter of the word is cut off

explanation.surface: A thinker of the past keeps agreeing to disagree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts AGREEING to AGREEIN, and 'to differ' rearranges that. John Scotus Erigena was a ninth-century Irish theologian.
explanation.definitionFit: John Scotus Erigena was a ninth-century Irish theologian and Neoplatonist thinker.

clue.text: Enliven article that is dull at heart

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: at heart puts the word for dull in the middle of the letters for that is

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
mat (matt) means dull, not shiny

explanation.surface: Liven up an essay whose centre is boring.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring to life or make lively is to put spirit and movement into something.

clue.text: One or two books for college

definitions.meaning: the Old Testament has First and Second ..., two books
... is a college at Cambridge and in London

explanation.definitionFit: The Bible's two books of royal history share the name with King's College, Cambridge.

clue.text: It was available for French travel industry

definitions.text: It was available for French travel
definitions.meaning: a stagecoach that once carried passengers across France
industry in the sense of hard work and application

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a French public stagecoach and steady, careful effort.
